                                                                2683

 1  last section.

 2               THE SECRETARY:   Section 2.  This

 9               SENATOR RIVERA:   Thank you, 

10  Mr. President, to explain my vote.

11               This is a bill much like ones that 

12  we've voted on in weeks past and sessions past 

13  that deals with sex offenders but yet does not 

14  make the distinction by levels.  

15               There is another bill on the agenda 

16  today that does something different; however, it 

17  has the same problem.

18               As I've stated many times on the 

19  floor, I certainly believe that it is our 

20  responsibility to secure citizens from 

21  predators.  But when we establish rules -- bills 

22  like this, when we try to establish laws of this 

23  kind which are so broad and do not have the 

24  distinctions that are already established in law, 

25  when someone is a sex offender and has served 

                                                                2684

 1  their time, then we create a law that is too 

 2  broad and that certainly I believe has more of a 

 3  punitive effect.  

 4               Which, again, as I've stated, can 

 5  certainly be warranted for certain people that 

 6  are considered sex offenders, but certainly not 

 7  Level 1's.  

 8               Since this does not have that 

 9  distinction, I'll be voting in the negative.

10               Thank you, Mr. President.

23               This is the second bill that we're 

24  going to deal with today that deals with sex 

25  offenders.  

                                                                2686

 1               This one in particular, what it 

 2  would do is it would eliminate, for all intents 

 3  and purposes, the levels that I was just speaking 

 4  about.  To me, this is probably -- this is 

 5  extremely egregious because it does not make the 

 6  distinction between someone that is a predator 

 7  and someone who is not.  

 8               It would make a person a sex 

 9  offender, regardless of the level, actually 

10  regardless of the offense.  There would be no 

11  levels anymore.  So this person, anybody who was 

12  convicted of a sex offense, would have to 

13  register for the rest of their lives.

14               Now, while I think that certainly 

15  predators that are Level 3's currently need to 

16  have this -- we need to make sure that we know 

17  where they are, we certainly should restrict 

18  where they work or where they can go -- when 

19  we're talking about a Level 1 sex offender, that 

20  distinction -- there is a reason why that 

21  distinction exists.  

22               This law would again make it too 

23  broad a definition.  I believe that we should be 

24  very careful about how we establish these levels 

25  on all the bills that deal with sex offenses.  I 

                                                                2687

 2  legislation.
